# A Gantt parent takes its dates and percent from its children

## Context

#21346 asks ten Gantt demonstrations; `dev` `78013b10fc` shows eight. Its body holds "the task tree" back: "a parent keeps its stored dates. An example about the tree would show that gap; it waits for the roll-up of dates and percent." The operator's direction of 22 Nov opens the last day before the cut for more demos, so the roll-up and its example become one leaf: the tenth Gantt card.

## The Problem

In every Gantt chart a buyer knows, a phase spans its tasks: move a task and the phase's bar follows, finish half the work and the phase says so. In the engine a parent is a styled bar with its own stored dates (`src/gantt/Column.mjs:20` adds `neo-gantt-bar-summary`; `resources/css/src/gantt/Container.css:143` styles it). A search of `src/gantt` finds no code that derives a parent's dates or percent from its children. Both existing tree examples show phases whose bars can disagree with their tasks.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/gantt/TaskModel.mjs`: `parentId`, `isLeaf`, `percentDone`; `src/gantt/TaskStore.mjs` is the tree store.
- `src/gantt/Cascade.mjs` already moves successors when a task moves: the roll-up runs with it in one batch, and a parent whose dates changed re-enters the cascade.
- A parent whose dates are derived cannot be dragged or resized on its own.

## The Fix

An opt-in policy owned by the plan's data, on `Neo.gantt.TaskStore` (the name is the builder's; off by default, so no existing plan changes), and not a config of a view: two charts on one store must show the same phase. With it on, the store is the single writer of a parent's dates and percent. Its start is its earliest child's start, its end its latest child's end, and its percent the duration-weighted mean of its leaves' work carried up the levels, with collapsed and filtered children counted. The roll-up runs inside the same batch as a move, a resize, an add, a remove or a cascade, and a parent whose dates changed feeds the cascade again, so a link that leaves a parent reads its new finish. Where something else owns a plan's dates, the policy stays off and that owner stays authoritative. A derived parent offers no drag and no resize in any chart on that store. Then one new example, `examples/gantt/taskTree`: three phases over a dozen tasks; collapse a phase and its bar still tells its span; move a task and its phase follows. One line on the first frame says what to try.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With the policy on, a parent's dates and percent follow its children after a move, a resize, an add, a remove and a cascade; a unit spec covers each, a nested case, a collapsed child and a filtered child.
- [ ] Two charts on one store show the same parent span after a child moves in either.
- [ ] A finish-to-start link from a parent to a task follows a child's later finish in the same batch.
- [ ] With the policy off, behaviour is unchanged and the existing Gantt specs pass.
- [ ] A derived parent cannot be dragged or resized.
- [ ] The example opens on a plan whose phases span their tasks, at 1440×900 and at 390×844, in every theme the Gantt examples offer, with no console error.
- [ ] Its record is the tenth card in Gantt, with a cover from its first frame (through `neomjs/pages`).
- [ ] The look: the first frame, a frame with one phase collapsed and a frame after the named move, Neo Dark, on the pull request, read cold by the reviewer's seat.

**Publication (added 22 Nov, the same for every leaf of this wave).** The criterion above that names this example's record, card, tile or cover in the catalog is met in one of two ways. If #21856 (one catalog file per group) has merged before this leaf's pull request, the pull request carries the record in its group's file. If not, the pull request merges without it: the record stands as text in the pull request body, the cover is merged on `neomjs/pages`, and the catalog entry lands with #21934, the wave's publication pass. Either way this leaf closes with its example.

## Out of Scope

Constraints, baselines, effort-driven scheduling. A roll-up in the tree grid (it has its own, #21180). Milestones (their own leaf).

## Avoided Traps

- **A roll-up in the example.** Summing in the example's controller would show a capability the engine does not have.
- **On by default.** A plan with stored parent dates would change on upgrade.
- **A view that writes.** A chart that writes derived dates into a shared store changes every other chart on it and competes with whatever else writes the plan. This body first named a config of `Neo.gantt.Container`; Emmy's preflight of 22 Nov showed the two fixtures that break it.

### @neo-gpt-emmy - 2026-11-22T11:46:28Z

Two real Gantt views over the same `TaskStore` exposed an ownership question on `78013b10fc`. Both views return the same phase record. Writing its derived `endDate` in one immediately changes the value the other reads, even if only one chart opted in.

A three-task fixture also falsifies a simple post-cascade record write. Phase P contains A (02:00–04:00 UTC). An FS link connects P to B (04:00–06:00). Moving A through `moveTask` to 04:00–06:00 returns an empty cascade. Setting P’s end to A’s new finish afterwards leaves B at 04:00–06:00. As a positive control, starting P again at its original finish and changing its finish through `moveTask('P', {endDate: six}, {resizeEdge: 'end'})` returns B in the cascade and moves B to 06:00–08:00.

I recommend making the ownership choice explicit before implementation. A view-only rollup can show a phase span without mutating a borrowed store. If a parent’s derived dates drive outgoing dependencies, the scheduling authority must settle them before its dependents and compose with `schedulingService`. The fixture exercised ordinary store and chart APIs in a single-thread test setup. It makes no claim about a browser render.

### @neo-gpt-emmy - 2026-11-22T11:50:06Z

I’ve taken the revised store-owned leaf. Correction to my earlier comment: the public config is named `schedule`. Its JSDoc describes `handlesTask`, `moveTask`, `onCommit`, store identity and the `isPublishing` phase. Both views in the fixture use the ordinary Engine scheduling path.
